title: The Kidneys and Waste
hook: Your two fist-sized kidneys filter your entire blood supply dozens of times a day, skimming out waste and fine-tuning exactly how much water and salt your body keeps.
key_points: The kidneys filter waste products and excess substances out of the blood.
What they remove leaves the body as urine; clean blood is returned to circulation.
They balance the body's water and salt levels, keeping the internal environment stable.
Each kidney holds about a million tiny filtering units called nephrons.
content_html: Tucked against your back, just below the ribs, sit two kidneys, each about the size of a fist. Their job sounds humble — they make urine — but what that really means is they continuously clean your blood, deciding moment to moment what stays in your body and what gets flushed out.
extra_html: As NIH's NIDDK explains, blood flows into each kidney and passes through roughly a million microscopic filters called nephrons. These strain out waste products like urea, along with excess water and salt, sending them onward to the bladder as urine while returning the cleaned blood to circulation. Just as important, the kidneys are master regulators of balance: if you drink a lot, they make more dilute urine; if you are dehydrated, they conserve water and concentrate it. By controlling water and salt levels — and keeping blood from becoming too acidic — the kidneys are central to homeostasis, the body's steady internal state.

related.title: The Circulatory System
related.hook: Your heart pumps blood through roughly 60,000 miles of vessels, delivering oxygen and fuel to every cell and hauling waste away — about once a minute.

related.title: Homeostasis: Staying Balanced
related.hook: Your body works hard to keep its inside world steady — temperature, water, blood sugar — no matter what's happening outside. That balancing act is homeostasis.

related.title: What Blood Does
related.hook: Blood looks like a single red liquid, but it's really a fleet of specialized parts — each cell type and the fluid itself carrying out a different life-sustaining job.

flashcards.prompt: What is the kidneys' main job?
flashcards.back_html: To filter the blood — removing waste products and extra water, which leave the body as urine, while clean blood is returned to circulation.

flashcards.prompt: Besides removing waste, what else do the kidneys regulate?

choices.text: The body's balance of water and salt
The amount of oxygen in the lungs
The speed of digestion in the stomach

flashcards.explanation_html: Kidneys fine-tune how much water and salt the body keeps versus excretes, a key part of maintaining a stable internal environment.

flashcards.prompt: What are the tiny filtering units inside each kidney called?
flashcards.explanation_html: Each kidney contains about a million nephrons, the microscopic structures that actually do the filtering of the blood.
